---
title: "📝 Assessment report: Word, LaTeX and PDF"
description: >
  fao_report(): an assessment report of an FAO fishing area in Chinese or English in one call,
  as Word, LaTeX or PDF. Its contents, arguments, sections and their settings, format, citation styles, the
  CMSY++ part, the tables it returns and the templates of its text.
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
source("_setup.R")
```

```{r data-source, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
data_source()
```

`fao_report()` writes the assessment report of one FAO major fishing area as a Word file (and,
if asked, as LaTeX and PDF), in Chinese or English, in one call. It runs the analyses of the package on the area, writes their
results into text made from templates, adds the charts and tables with numbered captions, and lists
the references it cites.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
fao_report(27)                                                  # language of fao_settings()
fao_report("Atlantic, Northeast", lang = "zh", author = "Hongyu Lin")
fao_report(27, lang = "en", font = "Times New Roman", citation = "fao")
```

::: callout-note
The report is a first draft. The parts only the author can write, such as other data sources,
the discussion of the conclusions and other references, are marked in grey with
"To be completed" ("待补充" in Chinese reports). Check the generated text before you use it.
:::

## 🚀 A first report

```{r}
report <- fao_report(27, file = "FAO27_report_en.docx", lang = "en")
report
```

The area is given by its code (`27`) or its English name (`"Atlantic, Northeast"`). The
call takes about half a minute and reports its progress in messages (hidden on this page): each
analysis, then the file written. Without `file`, the report is saved as
`reports/FAO27_report_en.docx` in the working directory; on this page the working directory is a
temporary folder.

The analyses run in a temporary folder of their own, with charts at 300 dpi and no PowerPoint
files. The charts end up in the Word file only, so the report leaves no chart files in your
folder; run the analysis functions themselves to keep them (see
[🌊 Fishing area analysis](fishing-areas.html)).

`fao_report()` returns the tables of the report invisibly, so assign the result. The main species
of the last five years:

```{r}
show_table(report$main_species, digits = 1)
```

## 📑 What the report contains

In this order:

1. **Cover**, on its own page without a page number: the project ("Project Report" unless
   `project` is given), the title, the report number, the author, the affiliation (only if given)
   and the date.
2. **Title block**: "Report 1" ("报告一" in Chinese reports, with Chinese numerals), the title and
   the author, centred.
3. **Abstract**: one paragraph with the area, the years and release of the FAO data, the topics
   and methods of the sections switched on, one sentence of results for the total catch, the main
   species, the main country, the stock status and CMSY++ (when these sections are on), and a
   closing recommendation.
4. **1 Data and methods**
    - **1.1 Data sources**: the FAO Global Capture Production release used, the date FAO published
      it, the date it was downloaded and the link to the file; the years, and the numbers of
      countries and species items in the area; the ASFIS list of species, the FAO yearbook of
      statistics, and how coastal countries are defined. A grey note asks for other data sources
      (regional fisheries management organisations, national agencies, Sea Around Us, ...).
    - **1.2 Methods**: one paragraph for each method used by the sections switched on
      (breakpoints, Mann-Kendall trend tests, stock status plots, diversity indices, ...), with its
      references, and a last paragraph on the software (R and faofishingreport).
5. **2 Results and conclusions**: one numbered subsection (2.1, 2.2, ...) for each section
   switched on, with its text, figures and tables. The last subsection, **Conclusions**, has one
   numbered conclusion per section, (1), (2), ..., and a grey note asking to complete them with
   stock assessments, the literature and management measures.
6. **3 Stock assessment of the main species (CMSY++)**, with `cmsy = TRUE` only: an overview,
   one subsection per species and a summary (see [📉 CMSY++ assessment](#cmsy)).
7. **References**: the references cited in the text, then a grey note on how to add others.
8. **Appendix**: mean yearly catch by decade of the main species (Table A1) and of the main
   countries (Table A2), and with CMSY++ the reference points, the priors and their sources
   (Tables A3 to A5).

The grey notes are the paragraphs the author has to write or check: other data sources, the
conclusions, other references, the comparison of each CMSY++ assessment with other assessments,
and the preferred temperatures of the species of the mean temperature of the catch. If a chart
could not be drawn, the report has "[Figure not available]" in its place.

## 🔎 Inside the Word file

Every paragraph of the report has a named Word style ("FAO Body", "FAO Heading 1", ...). The
format of the whole report can be changed in Word by modifying a style, and the file can be read
back in R with the officer package:

```{r}
word <- officer::docx_summary(officer::read_docx(report$file))
word <- word[word$content_type == "paragraph", ]
table(word$style_name)
```

The headings, styles "FAO Heading 1" and "FAO Heading 2":

```{r}
outline <- function(word) {
  headings <- word[word$style_name %in% c("FAO Heading 1", "FAO Heading 2"), ]
  cat(paste0(ifelse(headings$style_name == "FAO Heading 2", "    ", ""), headings$text), sep = "\n")
}
outline(word)
```

The abstract, the first "FAO Body" paragraph after the heading "Abstract":

```{r}
after_heading <- seq_len(nrow(word)) > which(word$style_name == "FAO Abstract Heading")
abstract <- word$text[after_heading & word$style_name == "FAO Body"][1]
show_table(data.frame(abstract))
```

The captions of the figures and tables, numbered by report:

```{r}
captions <- word[word$style_name %in% c("FAO Caption", "FAO Table Caption"), ]
show_table(data.frame(style = captions$style_name, caption = captions$text), n = 20)
```

The grey notes:

```{r}
show_table(data.frame(note = word$text[word$style_name == "FAO Note"]))
```

And the list of references, style "FAO Reference":

```{r}
show_table(data.frame(reference = word$text[word$style_name == "FAO Reference"]), n = 30)
```

## 🧾 Arguments

| Argument | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `area` | (required) | The FAO major fishing area: its code, e.g. `27`, or its English name, e.g. `"Atlantic, Northeast"`. An unknown area gives an error that lists the marine areas. |
| `...` | | Settings of the analyses, named with the section as prefix, e.g. `species_h_value = 0.2` (see [⚙️ Settings of the analyses](#settings)) |
| `file` | `reports/FAO<code>_report_<lang>.docx` | The file to write; its folder is created if needed. The other formats get the same name with `.tex` and `.pdf`. |
| `format` | `"docx"` | One or more of `"docx"`, `"latex"` and `"pdf"` (see [🖨️ Word, LaTeX and PDF](#formats)) |
| `lang` | `NULL`: the language of `fao_settings()` | `"zh"` (Chinese) or `"en"` (English); `"both"` gives a Chinese report |
| `title` | made from the area | e.g. "Assessment of Marine Capture Production in FAO Major Fishing Area 27 (Atlantic, Northeast)" |
| `report_no` | `1` | Number of the report: "Report 1" ("报告一" in Chinese reports, with Chinese numerals up to 99), and the first number of the figures and tables (Figure 1-1, Table 1-1) |
| `author` | `NULL`: "Author" | The author on the cover, under the title and in the properties of the file |
| `affiliation` | `NULL`: no line | The affiliation on the cover |
| `project` | `NULL`: "Project Report" | The text at the top of the cover ("课题报告" in Chinese reports) |
| `date` | `Sys.Date()` | The date on the cover, written as YYYY-MM-DD; also the access date in the references to R and faofishingreport |
| `font` | `NULL`: "Times New Roman" in Chinese reports, "Arial" in English reports | The font of Latin script and numbers; in English reports, of all text |
| `font_zh` | `"FangSong"` | The Chinese font of the body text, title, tables and references; headings and captions stay in SimHei and KaiTi |
| `citation` | `"apa"` | Citation style of English reports: `"apa"` or `"fao"`. Chinese reports always use numbered citations (GB/T 7714). |
| `top_n` | `10` | Number of main species and countries in the tables and charts, and of species assessed with CMSY++ (unless `cmsy_top` is given) |
| `data_version` | `"latest"` | The FAO release to use, as in `load_fao_data()` |
| `total`, `species`, `countries`, `groups`, `status`, `quality`, `diversity`, `fleets` | `TRUE` | Sections switched on by default (see [🧩 Sections](#sections)) |
| `shocks`, `collapse`, `synchrony`, `pelagic`, `mtc`, `distant` | `FALSE` | Sections switched off by default |
| `cmsy` | `FALSE` | `TRUE` adds a CMSY++ assessment of the main species; the result of an earlier run can also be given (see [📉 CMSY++ assessment](#cmsy)) |

## 🧩 Sections {#sections}

Each analysis is a section of the report, switched on or off with the argument of the same name.
The settings of its function are given with the prefix in the last but one column, and the last
column lists the references its text cites (full references at the end of this page).

| Switch | Default | Section of the report | Function | Prefix | References cited |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `total` | `TRUE` | Catch trends and stages: total catch with its breakpoints, 10-year trend, share of the world's marine catch | `fishing_area_data()` | `total_` | Bai and Perron (2003), Zeileis et al. (2003), Mann (1945), Kendall (1975) |
| `species` | `TRUE` | Main species of the last five years: table, charts, breakpoints and 10-year trends | `fishing_area_species()` | `species_` | as `total` |
| `countries` | `TRUE` | Main fishing countries of the last five years: table, charts, map, breakpoints and trends | `fishing_area_country()` | `countries_` | as `total` |
| `groups` | `TRUE` | Composition by ISSCAAP species group in the last year | `species_group_composition()` | `groups_` | none |
| `status` | `TRUE` | Stock status plots | `stock_status()` | `status_` | Kleisner et al. (2013) |
| `quality` | `TRUE` | Data quality: reported and estimated catch, taxonomic level | `data_quality()` | `quality_` | none |
| `diversity` | `TRUE` | Diversity and concentration of the catch (Shannon index, HHI) | `diversity_concentration()` | `diversity_` | Shannon (1948), Rhoades (1993) |
| `fleets` | `TRUE` | Catch of coastal countries and distant-water fleets | `coastal_distant()` | `fleets_` | none |
| `shocks` | `FALSE` | Catch shocks | `catch_shocks()` | `shocks_` | Cottrell et al. (2019), or Gephart et al. (2017) with `shocks_method = "gephart2017"` |
| `collapse` | `FALSE` | Fishery collapses, compared with random series | `collapse_analysis()` | `collapse_`, and `collapse_seed` | Mullon et al. (2005), or Worm et al. (2006) with `collapse_method = "worm2006"`; Wilberg and Miller (2007) |
| `synchrony` | `FALSE` | Synchrony of the catch and portfolio effect | `catch_synchrony()` | `synchrony_` | Loreau and de Mazancourt (2008), Thibaut and Connolly (2013), Carlson and Satterthwaite (2011), Ong et al. (2021), Lepš et al. (2019) |
| `pelagic` | `FALSE` | Pelagic to demersal ratio (P/D) | `pelagic_demersal()` | `pelagic_` | Caddy (1993) and de Leiva Moreno et al. (2000), or Grainger and Garcia (1996) with `pelagic_definition = "grainger_garcia"`; Hondorp et al. (2010) |
| `mtc` | `FALSE` | Mean temperature of the catch | `mean_temperature_catch()` | `mtc_` | Cheung et al. (2013), FishBase (Froese and Pauly), Huang et al. (2017) with the ERSST v5 data, Pyper and Peterman (1998), Alajmi et al. (2024) |
| `distant` | `FALSE` | Profiles of the main distant-water countries in the area | `distant_water_profile()` | `distant_`, and `distant_countries` | Swartz et al. (2010), Garibaldi and Limongelli (2003) |
| `cmsy` | `FALSE` | Stock assessment of the main species, a part of its own | `cmsy_area()` (and `cmsy_input()`) | `cmsy_` | Froese et al. (2023), Froese et al. (2017), FishBase (Froese and Pauly), Plummer (2003), FAO (2026b) |

Every report also cites the FAO release used, the FAO yearbook of statistics (FAO 2026a), R and
faofishingreport. The analyses themselves are described on the other pages of this site:
[🌊 Fishing area analysis](fishing-areas.html),
[📈 Composition, stock status and trends](status-trends.html),
[🔍 Data quality, diversity and fleets](quality-diversity-fleets.html),
[🌡️ Sea temperature and catch temperature](sst-mtc.html) and
[📉 CMSY++ stock assessment](cmsy.html).

The rest of the report follows the sections switched on:

- the **abstract** lists their topics and methods, and has a sentence of results for `total`,
  `species`, `countries`, `status` and `cmsy`;
- **1.2 Methods** has the paragraphs of their methods only (`groups`, `quality` and `fleets` need
  none);
- the subsections of **2 Results and conclusions** and the figures and tables are numbered in the
  order of the sections, and the **conclusions** have one item per section;
- the **references** list only what the text cites, e.g. Shannon (1948) only with `diversity`;
- the **appendix** has Tables A1 and A2 only with `species` and `countries`, and the CMSY++
  tables only with `cmsy`.

The total catch is always analysed, as it gives the data of the area, but its section is written
only with `total = TRUE`.

## 🎛️ Fewer or more sections

Three sections switched off, the pelagic to demersal ratio switched on, and stock status plots
with smoothed catches:

```{r}
short <- fao_report(27, file = "FAO27_short.docx", lang = "en", quality = FALSE, diversity = FALSE,
                    fleets = FALSE, pelagic = TRUE, status_smooth = TRUE)
short
short_word <- officer::docx_summary(officer::read_docx(short$file))
outline(short_word)
```

The results now have six subsections and the conclusions six items. The abstract and the methods
name the P/D ratio, and the references have Caddy (1993), de Leiva Moreno et al. (2000) and
Hondorp et al. (2010) instead of Shannon (1948) and Rhoades (1993):

```{r}
show_table(data.frame(reference = short_word$text[short_word$style_name == "FAO Reference"]), n = 30)
```

::: callout-note
The methods paragraphs describe the default settings of each analysis, e.g. the inclusion
criteria of the stock status plots and a minimum segment of 15% for the breakpoints. When you
change such settings (`status_smooth = TRUE`, `status_min_catch = 10000`,
`species_h_value = 0.2`, ...), the results follow them; describe the change in 1.2 Methods
yourself.
:::

## ⚙️ Settings of the analyses {#settings}

The function of each section has its own arguments. Give them to `fao_report()` with the name of
the section and "_" in front: `species_h_value = 0.2` is `h_value = 0.2` of
`fishing_area_species()`. Your settings win over the values the report sets.

| In `fao_report()` | Goes to | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `species_h_value = 0.2` | `fishing_area_species(h_value = 0.2)` | Breakpoints of the main species with a minimum segment of 20% of the series |
| `countries_line_linewidth = 1` | `fishing_area_country(line_linewidth = 1)` | Thinner lines in the charts of the countries |
| `status_smooth = TRUE` | `stock_status(smooth = TRUE)` | 3-year running mean of the catch before the stocks are classified |
| `status_min_catch = 10000` | `stock_status(min_catch = 10000)` | Only stocks with a total catch of at least 10 000 t |
| `shocks_method = "gephart2017"` | `catch_shocks(method = "gephart2017")` | Shocks as defined by Gephart et al. (2017), with its methods text and reference |
| `collapse_method = "worm2006"` | `collapse_analysis(method = "worm2006")` | Collapses as defined by Worm et al. (2006): methods, results, chart and conclusion change |
| `collapse_seed = 2` | the random number generator, before `collapse_analysis()` | Other random series for the null model (default 1, so the report gives the same numbers every time); the random state of the session is restored afterwards |
| `synchrony_by = "country"` | `catch_synchrony(by = "country")` | Synchrony of the countries instead of the species |
| `pelagic_definition = "grainger_garcia"` | `pelagic_demersal(definition = "grainger_garcia")` | Groups of Grainger and Garcia (1996) |
| `mtc_version = "builtin"` | `mean_temperature_catch(version = "builtin")` | The report default: FishBase data bundled with the package, nothing downloaded |
| `mtc_version = "latest"` | `mean_temperature_catch(version = "latest")` | The latest FishBase release, downloaded if needed |
| `distant_countries = 5` | `distant_water_profile()`, once per country | Profiles of the five countries with the largest distant-water catch in the area over the last five years (default 3), or of the countries named, e.g. `distant_countries = c("Russian Federation", "Belize")` |
| `cmsy_top = 5` | `cmsy_area(top = 5)` | Five species assessed with CMSY++ (default `top_n`) |
| `cmsy_settings = list(n.iter = 100000)` | `cmsy_area(settings = ...)` | CMSY++ settings, see `cmsy_defaults()` |

`collapse_seed` and `distant_countries` are settings of the report itself. The `cmsy_` prefix
also takes the arguments of `cmsy_input()`, such as `cmsy_min_years`. The arguments that the report
sets itself (`area`, `area_data`, `area_name`, `lang`, `pptx` and `table`) cannot be given.
Settings of a section that is switched off have no effect.

A setting must be named, start with the name of a section, and be an argument of the section's
function. Otherwise `fao_report()` stops before any analysis is run, and the error lists what is
allowed:

```{r, error = TRUE}
fao_report(27, species_h = 0.2)
fao_report(27, speceis_h_value = 0.2)
```

## 📐 Format {#format}

Chinese reports follow the usual format of Chinese project reports:

| Element | Format |
|---|---|
| Page | A4, portrait; margins 2.54 cm at top and bottom, 3.17 cm left and right |
| Body text | FangSong for Chinese and Times New Roman for Latin script and numbers, size 12 (小四), line spacing 1.5, first-line indent of two characters, justified |
| Title block | "报告一" and the title in FangSong, size 18 (小二), bold, centred; the author below in size 12 |
| "摘　要" | SimHei, size 15 (小三), centred |
| Section headings (1, 2, ...) | SimHei, size 14 (四号) |
| Subsection headings (1.1, 2.1, ...) | KaiTi, size 14 (四号) |
| Captions | SimHei, size 12 (小四), centred, numbered by report: 图1-1 below the figure, 表1-1 above the table; 附表1 in the appendix |
| Tables | Three-line tables (top and bottom rules of 1.5 pt, a rule of 0.75 pt below the header), FangSong and Times New Roman size 10.5 (五号), single line spacing |
| Citations | Superscript numbers in square brackets, in the order of first citation: [1], [3,4], [5-7] (GB/T 7714) |
| References | Numbered [1], [2], ... in the order of citation, GB/T 7714 format, with a hanging indent |
| Spaces | No spaces between Chinese characters and Latin letters or numbers, except after the number of a heading or caption ("2.1 渔获量变化与阶段划分", "图1-1 ...") |
| Page numbers | Centred in the footer, size 10.5 (五号); none on the cover, 1 on the title page |
| Cover | Project in SimHei size 26 (一号) bold, title size 22 (二号) bold, other lines size 16 (三号) |

English reports have the same page, structure, numbering and tables, in one font for all text,
Arial unless `font` is given (e.g. `font = "Times New Roman"`). Headings are bold, size 14 for
sections and 12 for subsections. Captions start with a bold label: "**Figure 1-1.** Catch in ...",
"**Table 1-1.** Main species items ...". Citations are author-date, in APA style (default) or in
the style of FAO publications (`citation = "fao"`).

In both languages, scientific names of species and genera are in italics, in the text and in the
tables: *Sardina pilchardus*, *Trachurus* spp. (with "spp." upright). Names of families and higher
groups stay upright, e.g. Actinopterygii. Symbols are in italics as well (*P* < 0.05, *H*). The
grey notes and the references are written as they are, without the Chinese spacing rule.

The headings have outline levels 1 and 2, so they show in the navigation pane of Word and in a
table of contents inserted in Word. The title and author are also stored in the properties of
the file.

## 🖨️ Word, LaTeX and PDF {#formats}

`format` chooses the files to write: `"docx"` (default), `"latex"` and `"pdf"`, one or more. The
analyses run once, and all formats have the same text, figures, tables, captions and references.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
fao_report(27, lang = "zh", format = c("docx", "pdf"))      # Word and PDF
fao_report(27, lang = "en", format = "latex")                # the LaTeX source only
report <- fao_report(27, format = c("docx", "latex", "pdf"))
report$file                                                  # named docx, latex and pdf
```

| `format` | Files written (for `fao_report(27, lang = "zh")`) | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `"docx"` | `reports/FAO27_report_zh.docx` | The Word file described in this article |
| `"latex"` | `reports/FAO27_report_zh.tex` and the folder `reports/FAO27_report_zh_figures/` | The XeLaTeX source of the same report, with its figures as PNG files. Chinese reports use the `ctexart` class, English reports the `article` class. |
| `"pdf"` | `reports/FAO27_report_zh.pdf` (and the `.tex`) | The LaTeX source compiled with XeLaTeX, with bookmarks for the headings |

The LaTeX version follows the format of the Word file (see [📐 Format](#format)): A4 pages with
the same margins, the same fonts and sizes, line spacing 1.5, three-line tables (booktabs, single
line spacing, columns sized to their contents and running over pages), numbered captions, the
cover without page number and pages numbered from 1 on the title page. The fonts are those
installed on the computer:

| | Windows | macOS | Linux |
|---|---|---|---|
| Chinese body text (仿宋) | FangSong | STFangsong | FandolFang (TeX Live) |
| Chinese headings and captions (黑体) | SimHei | Heiti SC | FandolHei |
| Chinese subsection headings (楷体) | KaiTi | Kaiti SC | FandolKai |
| Latin text and numbers | `font`: Times New Roman in Chinese reports, Arial in English reports (else Liberation Serif or Sans, else Latin Modern) | | |

Chinese fonts have no bold face: as in Word, bold Chinese text (the titles) is made by thickening
the strokes.

### Install TinyTeX (once) {#tinytex}

The PDF is compiled with XeLaTeX. The easiest way to get it is **TinyTeX**, a small TeX Live
distribution installed and kept up to date from R (Xie 2019). Run once:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
install.packages("tinytex")
tinytex::install_tinytex()     # downloads TinyTeX (about 100 MB) into your user folder
tinytex::is_tinytex()          # TRUE: R finds it
tinytex::tinytex_root()        # where it is installed
```

TinyTeX goes into `~/Library/TinyTeX` on macOS, `%APPDATA%/TinyTeX` on Windows and `~/.TinyTeX`
on Linux, and needs no administrator rights. Restart R after installing it. You do not need to
install any LaTeX package by hand: the first PDF report installs the ones it uses (ctex and xeCJK
for Chinese, booktabs, longtable, needspace, xurl, ...), which takes a few minutes once.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
fao_report(27, lang = "zh", format = "pdf")   # the first run also installs the LaTeX packages
```

| Situation | What to do |
|---|---|
| No LaTeX on the computer | `install.packages("tinytex")`, then `tinytex::install_tinytex()` |
| TinyTeX installed long ago; packages fail to install, or the message "Local TeX Live (2024) is older than remote repository" | `tinytex::reinstall_tinytex()` reinstalls the newest TinyTeX with the packages you had |
| Another TeX distribution (MacTeX, TeX Live, MiKTeX) | It is used if `xelatex` is on the system path; install missing packages with its own manager (e.g. `tlmgr install ctex`) |
| You changed the `.tex` file | Compile it again: `tinytex::xelatex("reports/FAO27_report_zh.tex")` |
| Only the LaTeX source is wanted | `format = "latex"` needs no LaTeX installation |

Without tinytex, the package calls `xelatex` from the system path (twice, for the bookmarks).

## 🔖 Citations and references

The references are listed only when the text cites them. The FAO release used, R and
faofishingreport are made from the data and the R session (release, publication and access dates,
versions); FishBase is cited with the version used when the report has CMSY++ or the mean
temperature of the catch; all other references come from `inst/extdata/report_references.csv`.

| Style | Citation in the text | List of references |
|---|---|---|
| Chinese reports, GB/T 7714 | superscript [7] | in the order of citation, numbered |
| `citation = "apa"`, APA 7th edition | (Kleisner et al., 2013); (Bai & Perron, 2003; Zeileis et al., 2003) | alphabetical; same authors and year as 2026a, 2026b |
| `citation = "fao"`, FAO publications | (Kleisner et al., 2013); (Bai and Perron, 2003) | alphabetical; same authors and year as 2026a, 2026b |

The same two references in each style, as the report writes them (FAO release 2026.1.0,
downloaded on 10 October 2026):

| Style | Kleisner et al. (2013) | FAO data |
|---|---|---|
| GB/T 7714 | Kleisner K, Zeller D, Froese R, et al. Using global catch data for inferences on the world's marine fisheries[J]. Fish and Fisheries, 2013, 14(3): 293-311. DOI: 10.1111/j.1467-2979.2012.00469.x. | FAO. FishStat: Global capture production 1950–2024 (release 2026.1.0)[DB/OL]. Rome: FAO, 2026[2026-10-10]. https://www.fao.org/fishery/static/Data/Capture_2026.1.0.zip. |
| APA | Kleisner, K., Zeller, D., Froese, R., & Pauly, D. (2013). Using global catch data for inferences on the world's marine fisheries. *Fish and Fisheries*, *14*(3), 293–311. https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1467-2979.2012.00469.x | FAO. (2026). *FishStat: Global capture production 1950–2024* (Release 2026.1.0) [Data set]. https://www.fao.org/fishery/static/Data/Capture_2026.1.0.zip |
| FAO | Kleisner, K., Zeller, D., Froese, R. & Pauly, D. 2013. Using global catch data for inferences on the world's marine fisheries. *Fish and Fisheries*, 14(3): 293–311. https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1467-2979.2012.00469.x | FAO. 2026. FishStat: Global capture production 1950–2024 (release 2026.1.0). [Accessed on 10 October 2026]. In: FishStatJ. Available at: https://www.fao.org/fishery/statistics/software/fishstatj/en. Licence: CC-BY-4.0. |

In GB/T 7714, the letter in square brackets gives the type of document: [J] journal article,
[M] book, [C] proceedings, [R] report, [DB/OL] online database, [CP/OL] online computer program;
up to three authors are listed, more as the first three and "et al.". The FAO style follows the
reference lists of FAO publications (e.g. FAO 2024), and cites FishStat data as these
publications do, with the access date, FishStatJ and the licence.

## 📉 CMSY++ assessment {#cmsy}

With `cmsy = TRUE`, the main species are also assessed with CMSY++ (`cmsy_area()`): the `top_n`
species items identified to species with the largest catch of the last ten years, or `cmsy_top` of
them. CMSY++ needs JAGS, installed once with `cmsy_setup()`; without it, `fao_report()` stops with
a message. The assessment takes a few minutes.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
cmsy_setup()                          # once: JAGS and the R packages of CMSY++
report <- fao_report(27, lang = "en", cmsy = TRUE)
report
#> FAO report: .../reports/FAO27_report_en.docx
#> Sections: total, species, countries, groups, status, quality, diversity, fleets, cmsy
#>   $main_species           main species of the last five years (10 rows)
#>   $main_countries         main fishing countries of the last five years (10 rows)
#>   $cmsy_reference_points  CMSY++ biological reference points with 95% confidence limits (10 rows)
#>   $cmsy_priors            CMSY++ priors, their sources and links (10 rows)
#>   $cmsy                   CMSY++ result (folder .../reports/cmsy/Atlantic__Northeast)
#>   $analyses               results of the analyses: total, species, ..., fleets, cmsy

View(report$cmsy_reference_points)    # r, k, MSY, Fmsy, Bmsy, B/Bmsy and F/Fmsy with 95% limits
View(report$cmsy_priors)              # priors, their sources and links

# 15 main species and countries in the tables, 5 species assessed, longer MCMC chains
fao_report(27, lang = "en", top_n = 15, cmsy = TRUE, cmsy_top = 5,
           cmsy_settings = list(n.iter = 100000))
```

The report then has an abstract sentence on the stocks, a methods paragraph on CMSY++, and a part
of its own after the results:

```
3 Stock assessment of the main species (CMSY++)
    3.1 Overview
    3.2 Atlantic herring (Clupea harengus)
    3.3 Blue whiting(=Poutassou) (Micromesistius poutassou)
    ...
    3.12 Summary
```

- **Overview**: how many species were assessed (and which could not be), how many stocks were
  maximally sustainably fished (B/Bmsy ≥ 0.8) or overfished (B/Bmsy < 0.8) in their last year, as
  in FAO (2026b), and how many lay in the green (B/Bmsy ≥ 1 and F/Fmsy ≤ 1) and red (B/Bmsy < 1
  and F/Fmsy > 1) quadrants of the Kobe plot; a table of the results (years, r, k, MSY, B/Bmsy,
  F/Fmsy, status), the Kobe plot and B/Bmsy of all stocks.
- **One subsection per species**: r, k and MSY with their 95% confidence limits, B/Bmsy and
  F/Fmsy in the last year, the catch as a percentage of MSY, the status, the probabilities of the
  four Kobe quadrants, the CMSY++ chart of the species, and a grey note asking to compare the
  result with other assessments and discuss the priors.
- **Summary**, and in the appendix: **Table A3** biological reference points (r, k, MSY, Fmsy,
  Bmsy, B/Bmsy, F/Fmsy) with 95% confidence limits, **Table A4** the priors (resilience, ranges of
  r and k, B/k priors of the first, an intermediate and the last year) and **Table A5** their
  sources (source of the r prior, source of the B/k priors, FishBase or SeaLifeBase page of the
  species), followed by the links to the FishBase data, the CMSY++ code and user guide, and the
  FAO data.

All CMSY++ results (input files, runs, charts and tables) are kept in the folder `cmsy/` next to
the report, e.g. `reports/cmsy/Atlantic__Northeast/`, with `cmsy_result.rds`. To write the
report again, e.g. with other sections or after editing the templates, give that result to
`cmsy` instead of `TRUE`; CMSY++ does not run again and the `cmsy_` settings are not used. The
result of `cmsy_area()` can be given in the same way:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
cmsy27 <- readRDS(file.path("reports", "cmsy", "Atlantic__Northeast", "cmsy_result.rds"))
fao_report(27, lang = "en", cmsy = cmsy27, pelagic = TRUE)

area27 <- cmsy_area("Atlantic, Northeast", top = 10)
fao_report(27, lang = "en", cmsy = area27)
```

The charts of the CMSY++ part come from the run, in the language it was run in. See
[📉 CMSY++ stock assessment](cmsy.html) for the method, its settings and its limits: FAO data
have catches only, so the results are indicative.

## 📦 What fao_report() returns {#returned}

A list of class `fao_report`, returned invisibly:

| Element | Content |
|---|---|
| `file` | Paths of the files written, named `docx`, `latex` and `pdf` |
| `sections` | The sections switched on |
| `main_species` | Main species of the last five years: name in the report language, English and scientific names, mean yearly catch (t), share of the catch (%), peak year, catch of the last year as % of the peak, 10-year trend ("up", "down" or "none") |
| `main_countries` | The same for the main fishing countries |
| `mtc_species` | With `mtc = TRUE`: the species of the mean temperature of the catch, their FishBase matches and preferred temperatures |
| `analyses` | The result of each analysis, named by section, e.g. `analyses$status` is the result of `stock_status()` |
| `cmsy` | With CMSY++: the full result of `cmsy_area()` |
| `cmsy_reference_points` | With CMSY++: one row per stock with r, k, MSY, Fmsy, Bmsy, B/Bmsy and F/Fmsy, each with its lower and upper 95% confidence limits (`_lcl`, `_ucl`), the last catch, the probabilities of the Kobe quadrants and the status |
| `cmsy_priors` | With CMSY++: resilience and its source, prior ranges of r and k, the MSY prior, the B/k priors with their sources, and links to the species page in FishBase or SeaLifeBase, the FishBase data, the CMSY++ user guide and the FAO data |

```{r}
names(report)
show_table(report$main_countries, digits = 1)
names(report$analyses)
stocks <- report$analyses$status$stocks
show_table(stocks[, c("species_name", "peak_year", "peak_tonnes", "pct_of_peak", "status_last_year")],
           n = 5, digits = 0)
```

## ✏️ Change the wording

All the text of the report comes from `inst/extdata/report_text.csv`, one row per piece of text
with the columns `key`, `en` and `zh`:

```{r}
texts <- read.csv(system.file("extdata", "report_text.csv", package = "faofishingreport"),
                  fileEncoding = "UTF-8", colClasses = "character")
nrow(texts)
show_table(data.frame(texts[texts$key %in% c("h_status", "status_p2", "concl_status"), ], row.names = NULL))
```

- `{last_year}`, `{oc_pct}`, ... are placeholders, filled in with the results. Keep to the
  placeholders of the original text: an unknown one stops the report with an error.
- `{cite:kleisner2013}` cites a reference by its key, `{cite:bai2003,zeileis2003}` several. It
  becomes a superscript number in Chinese reports and "(Kleisner et al., 2013)" in English
  reports.
- `*...*` is written in italics (`*P*`, scientific names), `^...^` as superscript and `~...~` as
  subscript, e.g. `HHI = ∑(100*p*~i~)^2^`.

The references are in `inst/extdata/report_references.csv`:

```{r}
refs <- read.csv(system.file("extdata", "report_references.csv", package = "faofishingreport"),
                 fileEncoding = "UTF-8", colClasses = "character")
show_table(refs[, c("key", "type", "author", "year", "title")], n = 5)
```

| Column | Content |
|---|---|
| `key` | The key used in `{cite:key}` |
| `type` | `J` journal article, `M` book, `C` paper in proceedings, `R` report in a series (e.g. FAO Fisheries Technical Paper). `DB` (database) and `CP` (computer program) are the types of the references the function makes itself: the FAO data, FishBase, R and faofishingreport. |
| `author` | Persons as "Family, I. I." separated by ";", or an organisation such as FAO |
| `year`, `title` | Year and title |
| `container` | Journal or proceedings |
| `volume`, `issue`, `pages` | Volume, issue and pages, e.g. `293-311` |
| `edition` | Number of the edition, e.g. `4` for "4th ed." |
| `series` | Series of a report or book, e.g. "FAO Fisheries Technical Paper No. 359" |
| `place`, `publisher` | Place and publisher |
| `doi`, `url` | DOI without "https://doi.org/", and web address |

To change the wording or add references, edit these files in the package source and reinstall
the package (e.g. `R CMD INSTALL .` in the source folder), then restart R: the files are read
once per session.
